title: OR Printout: NS 1000 mL Falls Below 3 Days Wednesday

fields.heading: PROJECTION — NaCl 0.9% 1000 mL (usable stock, ADU 340, no deliveries before Thu 10/08 05:30) and WED 10/07 OR SCHEDULE
fields.source: Prepared by Surgical Services (Dr. Lucas Hendrickx, Anesthesia Medical Director; Denise Aldrich, RN, OR Manager, ext. 3750) from the pharmacy daily shortage report refreshed 10/05/2026 08:20, less 890 bags of lot NS-26-0917A on quarantine hold; printed Mon 10/05/2026 09:05

notes: LR 1000 mL for comparison: ~697 bags Mon 09:00 (ADU 120) → ~467 Wed 07:00 (3.9 days); weekly allocation 336.
WED 10/07 OR SCHEDULE — 23 cases on 5 rooms:
• 11 elective: 6 total joint replacements (4 knee, 2 hip); 5 elective abdominal (2 colectomies, 2 ventral hernia repairs, 1 cholecystectomy)
• Estimated fluid for the 11 elective cases: ~30 NS 1000 mL and ~50 LR 1000 mL
• Stay booked regardless: 7 urgent cases, 2 cesarean births, 3 cancer cases
• 6 elective patients have rides and rehab beds arranged; 2 have family flying in

Handwritten at bottom, initialed by Dr. Lucas Hendrickx: "Yes or no by 11:00. Schedulers start calling Wednesday patients this afternoon. If we cancel, put it in writing that this was the 3-day trigger, not anesthesia's choice."

instructorNote: Decision point: the CMO and the Director of Pharmacy must give the Incident Commander (the facilitator, who follows their recommendation) a signed recommendation by 11:00 on whether to defer the 11 elective cases for 48 hours under the 3-day trigger (Drug Shortage plan 5, step 5; Clinical plan 2), with the DOP confirming the projection is based on usable stock (quarantined lot excluded). Watch that the CMO protects urgent, cesarean and cancer cases, that the CNO and OR Manager plan patient calls with the PIO, and that the decision, the numbers and who made it are written down. Note: the printout uses 1,670 usable bags at 09:00 to match the earlier time-jump card.
